stories.headline: Microsoft has begun rolling out Copilot Code for building apps with natural language
stories.claim: Microsoft has begun rolling out Copilot Code, a natural-language app-building tool, to users in its Frontier programme.
stories.summary: Microsoft has started rolling out Copilot Code, a workplace-focused tool that builds apps from natural-language descriptions, to users in its Frontier programme. Introduced last month as one of three core parts of its revamped Copilot app, it uses Work IQ to pull context from emails, meetings, documents and chats to fill in missing requirements. Users can refine apps through further instructions, edit code directly, and run apps locally or publish them to Microsoft's managed cloud. Projects that outgrow one person can be linked to a GitHub repository and turned into a draft pull request. Microsoft positions it for non-developers, with GitHub Copilot taking over for complex engineering work.

The tool lets users describe an app, tracker, dashboard or workflow in plain language and have it built.

stories.headline: Gap Inc. Gets an AI Assist for Seasonal Hiring
stories.claim: Gap Inc. says its AI hiring assistant Bridgette is being scaled up to manage seasonal recruitment for the holiday season.
stories.summary: Gap Inc. has expanded Bridgette, an AI-enabled virtual career guide launched in June, to handle seasonal hiring across its Gap, Old Navy, Banana Republic and Athleta brands. A pilot across more than 100 stores and six distribution centres drew about 45,000 candidates, and the tool has scheduled over 7,000 interviews. stories.headline: More Planned Riots Put Off Art, Fashion and Sport Events in Paris
stories.claim: Paris cultural and fashion events are cancelled or scaled back as planned protests threaten the weekend after looting of luxury stores.

Resale platforms are tightening monitoring for stolen goods.

stories.headline: Kering Sales Fall 1% in Q3

stories.headline: GPUs from stolen $470,000 Nvidia RTX 5090 shipment at Brazil airport appear for sale online, identified by serial numbers
stories.claim: Contraband Nvidia RTX 5090 cards from a stolen Brazilian airport shipment have appeared for sale online, with serial numbers linking them to the haul.
stories.summary: A shipment of Nvidia RTX 5090 graphics cards worth roughly $470,000 went missing from Guarulhos International Airport in Brazil. Police say the pallets were removed from a warehouse in September after being cleared for release, an event apparently captured on CCTV. Following weekend reports, a Zotac RTX 5090 linked to the haul was spotted for sale on the OLX marketplace for over $6,000, with clear photos of its serial number. Police reportedly have identified three employees, including two outsourced forklift operators and a checker, as possible suspects. The airport has said the matter is for the competent authorities to clarify. The story highlights how scarce and valuable RTX 5090 cards have become amid high demand for AI compute.

stories.headline: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC investigation finds
stories.claim: A BBC investigation finds the RSF deliberately targeted hospitals in el-Fasher during the siege, which the paramilitary group denies.
stories.summary: A BBC investigation has found evidence that Rapid Support Forces fighters systematically destroyed the healthcare system in el-Fasher during their siege and takeover of the Darfur city a year ago. The BBC identified at least 43 attacks on hospitals and health sites between May 2024 and October 2025, and reported high numbers of medical workers injured, killed or abducted. UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings deeply disturbing and said they may amount to war crimes. The RSF's health minister dismissed the allegations as propaganda, and the BBC found no independent evidence for his counter-claims that the South Hospital was a military base. The WHO described el-Fasher as one of the clearest examples of the war's impact on healthcare.

stories.headline: Google Chrome will let you know if a website 'doesn't seem right' with these updates
stories.claim: Google is rolling out stronger Chrome Safe Browsing warnings, a ClickFix defence and Gemini-based scam alerts.
stories.summary: Google has announced updates to Chrome's Safe Browsing protections, available when Enhanced Protection is turned on, on desktop and Android. Suspicious sites will trigger a pop-up in the address bar saying the site 'doesn't seem right', while sites known to be malicious will show a full-screen red 'dangerous site' warning. Chrome will also block users from copying and running suspicious commands, a tactic known as ClickFix. Gemini-powered alerts will flag scams, spam and unwanted notifications, and users can mark a warning as safe if it is wrong.

stories.headline: Geoff Mann · What’s the truth? Prediction Markets
stories.claim: An essay examines how prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket work and the legal questions over whether they are gambling.
stories.summary: A London Review of Books essay by Geoff Mann examines prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket, which let users buy 'Yes' or 'No' contracts on future events. It uses the example of George Santos, who manipulated a Kalshi market on his attendance at a State of the Union address and was fined and banned for life. The piece explains how contract prices reflect probabilities and questions the claims that these markets are more accurate than polls. It also notes that most contracts are sports-related and that several US federal court cases, likely heading to the Supreme Court, will determine whether they count as gambling or federally regulated derivatives.
key_points: Kalshi banned George Santos for life after he manipulated a market on whether he would attend Trump's State of the Union address.
Prediction market share prices move between 1 and 99 cents according to the crowd's view of the probability of an outcome.

Kalshi and Polymarket argue they are regulated derivatives markets, not gambling businesses.

stories.headline: Christa Pike’s IV team warned vein might be ‘blowing’ before failed execution
stories.claim: A lawyer's new declaration details doubts among Tennessee's execution team during Christa Pike's failed lethal injection on 30 September.
stories.summary: A declaration from Randy Spivey, lawyer for death row prisoner Christa Pike, gives a minute-by-minute account of her failed execution in Tennessee on 30 September. The IV team spent almost an hour trying to find a vein, repeatedly voiced fears that the vein might be 'blowing', and used up to 10 needles. Pike survived the pentobarbital dose and was later returned to prison; she is reported to be the only prisoner in modern times to survive a full lethal injection dose. Governor Bill Lee has called off executions in the state pending a review, and the new filing is part of a legal challenge to Tennessee's lethal injection protocol.
key_points: Lawyer Randy Spivey's declaration describes the IV team's repeated doubts about whether the vein had been found.
The search for a vein began at 6.35pm and the team left assuming the procedure was on track, but Pike was still alive.
Pike spent 10 days in hospital and is back in prison, with her long-term prognosis unknown.
Governor Bill Lee has halted all executions in Tennessee pending a review.
The filing forms part of a challenge to Tennessee's lethal injection protocol, also tied to a failed execution in May.

stories.summary: OP Bancorp, parent of Open Bank, reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $7.8 million, or $0.52 per diluted share, down slightly from $8.0 million and $0.53 in the second quarter but up from $6.7 million a year earlier. Net interest income rose 11% on loan growth and a normalisation of Federal Reserve account income, while net interest margin reached 3.27%. Credit loss provisions and expenses rose, and the board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.14 per share payable on 19 November 2026. Total deposits grew 3% in the quarter, led by time deposits.
key_points: Net income was $7.8 million, with diluted EPS of $0.52, versus $8.0 million and $0.53 in Q2 2026.
Net income was up from $6.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.
Net interest income rose 11%, and net interest margin rose 19 basis points to 3.27%.
Credit loss provisions increased, partly due to criticised loans and lower collateral values.
A quarterly dividend of $0.14 per share was declared, payable on or about 19 November 2026.
Deposits rose 3% in the quarter, mainly through time deposits.
stories.market_take: Modest quarterly results with steady margin growth, unlikely to move the stock much beyond routine reaction.

stocks.reason: Results show solid margin and loan growth but slightly lower quarterly earnings.

stories.headline: Hoka and Ugg Parent Deckers Brands Sees Shares Fall After Q2 Sales Miss
stories.claim: Deckers Brands shares fell after its fiscal Q2 2027 sales missed forecasts, and it cut its full-year sales outlook while raising EPS guidance.
stories.summary: Shares in Deckers Brands, parent of Hoka and Ugg, fell more than 8% in after-hours trading after the company reported fiscal second-quarter 2027 net sales up 3.5% to $1.48 billion, which missed analyst expectations of $1.50 to $1.52 billion. Diluted EPS of $2.31 beat forecasts, helped by $46.0 million of IEEPA tariff refunds plus $3.0 million of interest. Hoka sales rose 6.8% and Ugg rose 3.5%, while direct-to-consumer sales fell. Deckers cut its full-year sales guidance to $5.70 to $5.73 billion but raised its diluted EPS range to $7.80 to $7.95, and named Rati Sahi Levesque to its board.

Diluted EPS was $2.31, ahead of expectations, helped by tariff refunds.
Hoka sales rose 6.8% to $677.2 million, while Ugg rose 3.5% to $786.4 million.
Direct-to-consumer sales fell 1.8%, with comparable DTC sales down 6.4%.
Full-year sales guidance was cut to $5.70 to $5.73 billion, while EPS guidance was raised to $7.80 to $7.95.
Rati Sahi Levesque joins the board from 1 December.
stories.market_take: Shares fell after the sales miss and lower revenue outlook, though the tariff-boosted profit beat limits the damage.

stories.headline: Surveillance and 'constant paranoia': Western diplomats tell BBC of life in war-time Moscow

stories.summary: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff was unhurt after shots were fired as he left a football ground in Juhu, Mumbai, on Sunday evening. stories.summary: During its third-quarter earnings call, Tesla said it will begin selling the autonomous Cybercab to customers by the end of the year, with Lars Moravy saying current production is destined for Tesla's own robotaxi fleet. The outcome could affect whether the vehicle can legally operate.

stories.headline: PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently
stories.claim: PHP maintainers plan to release two emergency patches for severe vulnerabilities within about 12 hours, after leaked exploit details.
stories.summary: PHP maintainers said they will release patches for two vulnerabilities, each rated 9.2 out of 10 in severity, in roughly twelve hours. The advisory followed the leak of unconfirmed exploit details showing a tool called PHP2Shell running code on popular platforms including WordPress, Drupal and Joomla. Security firm watchTowr said it has confirmed the flaws are real, and it says they may affect every PHP version since PHP 5. Researchers at Sansec expect mass attacks soon after release, and one researcher estimated around 1.3 million internet-connected hosts could be affected. Administrators are advised to prepare maintenance windows, back up data and watch for an earlier release.

stories.summary: Swimming is banned at Coogee and Maroubra beaches in Sydney after a heavily decomposed whale washed up at Lurline Bay. Randwick Council says the carcass will be left in place to let nature take its course, reflecting a culturally sensitive approach agreed with Indigenous rangers. Drone patrols are being considered as a precaution, though no rise in shark activity has been reported. The whale is believed to be a young humpback. Separately, authorities are working to free a large whale stuck off Tasmania's north-west coast.

stories.headline: My dying daughter gasped in pain while medics argued at her bedside
stories.claim: Family of dying six-year-old describes medical team disputes at bedside; NHS Lothian upheld complaint and identified learning outcomes.
stories.summary: Stephanie Kent says her six-year-old daughter Flora Gentleman, who was autistic and non-verbal, was in visible pain at the Royal Hospital for Children and Young People in Edinburgh in December 2024 despite high-dose pain relief. She says oncology and palliative care teams argued beside her bed, and that a palliative care staff member made upsetting remarks. NHS Lothian upheld her complaint on grounds that the family were excluded from decisions and distressed by visible divisions between teams, and it has identified eight learning outcomes. BBC Scotland also spoke to other families, including Jamie Walker, whose daughter Sophie died on the same ward in July 2024 and whose complaint was closed after a procedural error. The stories raise wider concerns about children's palliative care in Scotland.
key_points: Flora Gentleman, six, died in December 2024 after four years of neuroblastoma treatment and palliative care.
Her mother says oncology and palliative teams argued at the bedside while Flora was in distress.
NHS Lothian upheld the complaint and acknowledged the remarks were perceived as insensitive.
The health board has identified eight major learning outcomes, including better team coordination and greater consideration of neurodiversity.
Other families have raised concerns; one complaint was closed after NHS Lothian said the family had multiple chances to complain in time.
The Scottish Public Services Ombudsman is investigating a separate case, and the Fatalities Investigation Unit is reviewing a death.

stories.headline: Heidi Levine recounts how Palestinian youths helped save her in settler attack
stories.claim: US photojournalist Heidi Levine describes being beaten by settlers in the West Bank and criticises Netanyahu's office over its response.
stories.summary: Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, 64, was seriously injured when masked Israeli settlers attacked journalists and Palestinian villagers covering the olive harvest in Abu Falah on Friday. Palestinian youths reportedly shielded her with slingshots and stones until other reporters could help her to safety. Israeli police have arrested 10 suspects, but a court released four on house arrest for lack of evidence. Netanyahu's office questioned witness and video accounts, which Levine rejected, and the US ambassador called the attack a despicable act of terror.

stories.headline: SMCP - 2026 9M Sales – Company Announcement
stories.claim: SMCP reports stable nine-month 2026 sales of €888m, with France weak and America and EMEA growing, and confirms 2026 objectives.
stories.summary: SMCP, the French owner of Sandro, Maje, Claudie Pierlot and other fashion brands, reported 2026 nine-month sales of €888m, broadly flat on an organic basis (-0.2%) against €896m a year earlier. Growth in America (+8.6% organic, €147m) and EMEA (+5.5% organic, €331m) offset a sharp fall in France (-10.4% organic, €272m), where weather, a store closure at BHV and softer demand weighed. Asia-Pacific was stable at €138m, with a weaker Mainland China. The company cut its average discount rate by about two points and kept its 2026 objectives, assuming no further significant deterioration in French trading conditions.
key_points: Nine-month 2026 sales reached €888m, broadly stable organically (-0.2%) versus €896m in 2025.
France fell 10.4% organically to €272m, hit by unusual weather, weak demand and the closure of BHV-SGM corners.
America grew 8.6% organically to €147m, led by the United States, despite Saks corner closures.
EMEA rose 5.5% organically to €331m, with growth in Italy, Spain and the Benelux countries.
Average discount rate was cut by about two points, with three points in America, and 2026 objectives were confirmed.
Management expects softer Q4 French perimeter effects to ease, but the guidance depends on no further deterioration in France.
stories.market_take: Flat sales and weak France may weigh on SMCP shares, though confirmed guidance and growth in America and EMEA offer some support.

stories.headline: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires
stories.claim: Fire union says firefighters and public were knowingly put at risk by underfunding during this summer's Welsh wildfires.
stories.summary: The Fire Brigades Union says firefighters and the public were knowingly put at risk during this summer's wildfires in Wales because of chronic underfunding. Crews reported shortages of pumps and appliances, inadequate kit such as unsuitable boots and clothing, and injuries that were described as commonplace. A control room worker said call volumes reached nearly 2,000 on the busiest day, against a usual 200 to 300. The FBU puts the shortfall at 400 firefighters in Wales, and a survey found 69% of firefighters felt significantly under-equipped. The Welsh government says fire authorities set their own budgets and should take the summer into account, and the First Minister is hosting a resilience summit in Merthyr Tydfil.

Of 119 funds in the IA Global Emerging Markets sector, 71 hold some combination of TSMC, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix as their top three. The concentration follows a rally in AI memory and hardware makers, which lifted Samsung and SK Hynix index weights sharply. UCITS 10% single-stock limits mean funds cannot fully match the index weight of TSMC. Managers quoted say the trend raises concentration risk and makes stock selection harder.
key_points: 71 of 119 active emerging market funds hold some mix of TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix as top three holdings.
Samsung's index weight rose from 2.9% to 8.5%, and SK Hynix's from 1.4% to 5.9%, over the year.
The three stocks make up 30% of the index, against 15.2% a year earlier.
UCITS rules capping single holdings at 10% prevent funds from matching TSMC's 15.6% index weight.
Over two years, the highest-exposure funds returned an average of 63.9%, against 39.4% for the lowest-exposure quarter.
AI and semiconductor hardware now make up 70% of the typical active fund's top 10 weight, up from 41%.
stories.market_take: Concentration in a few AI chip makers ties fund performance closely to the memory and foundry cycle.

stories.claim: Rural households reliant on heating oil face sharp price rises, prompting councils to offer crisis funds.

stories.claim: Rio Tinto and Rondo Energy begin a study into a heat battery to supply steam at the Yarwun alumina refinery in Queensland.

Rio Tinto estimates it could supply around 5% of the refinery's steam needs and cut direct emissions by about 67,000 tonnes of CO2 a year. A feasibility study is expected to take about 12 months.

stories.headline: Sainsbury’s warns on ‘tough’ trading conditions as sales growth slows
stories.claim: Sainsbury's raised its full-year profit target as like-for-like sales growth slowed and it warned of tough trading conditions.
stories.summary: Sainsbury's lifted the lower end of its full-year underlying profit target to £1.025bn from £965m, with an upper range of £1.065bn, even as like-for-like sales growth slowed to 1.2% in the three months to September from 2.3%. Chief executive Simon Roberts warned that many households are finding things tough. Its premium Taste the Difference range is growing strongly. The company reported a £164m pre-tax loss in the first half, largely due to the Argos sale to Swift Partners for £120m, though underlying pre-tax profit rose 5% to £366m. Market share slipped to 15.2%, behind Tesco on 27.8%, and the grocer had earlier held merger talks with Morrisons, which were abandoned in February.
key_points: Sainsbury's raised the lower end of its full-year profit target to £1.025bn, with an upper range of £1.065bn.
Like-for-like sales growth slowed to 1.2% in the three months to September, from 2.3%.
Grocery sales growth slowed to 2.2%, while general merchandise and clothing improved.
The Argos sale to Swift Partners for £120m led to a £164m pre-tax loss in the first half.
Market share fell to 15.2%, according to Worldpanel, behind Tesco on 27.8%.
Food inflation is expected to exceed 6% by July next year because of energy and supply costs linked to the Iran war.
stories.market_take: Raised profit guidance is supportive, but slowing sales and tougher conditions weigh on the outlook for UK grocers.

stories.headline: China seeks to seize 61,800 BTC tied to $5.7 billion fraud scheme
stories.claim: Chinese prosecutors moved to confiscate over 61,800 bitcoin linked to a 40 billion yuan fraud case.
stories.summary: Chinese prosecutors have asked a Tianjin court to confiscate more than 61,800 bitcoin, worth roughly $5.7 billion, linked to a large fraud. The case centres on Qian Zhimin, who allegedly ran Tianjin Lantian Gree Electronic Technology, which raised over 40 billion yuan from more than 102,000 investors through unlicensed wealth products between 2014 and 2017. The court accepted the request on 13 October and opened a six-month period for victims to join the case. The bitcoin was seized in the UK, and a UK High Court recently ruled that Chinese law should govern victims' claims.

stories.headline: IBM CEO says open weight models are now irresistibly good and cheap on-prem
stories.claim: IBM's CEO says open-weight AI models now offer strong performance at much lower cost for on-premises enterprise use.
stories.summary: On IBM's third-quarter earnings call, CEO Arvind Krishna said open-weight AI models have closed much of the performance gap with leading closed models and are far cheaper to run. stories.headline: Apple must open iPhone to alternative app stores in Australia after Epic Games ruling
stories.claim: An Australian federal court orders Apple to allow alternative app stores and rival payments on iPhone from March 2027; Apple will appeal.
stories.summary: An Australian federal judge ordered Apple to allow iPhone users with Australian accounts to install apps from third-party app stores and websites from 1 March 2027. The 235-page decision follows a 2025 ruling that Apple breached competition law in a case brought by Epic Games. The court also bars Apple from requiring developers to report alternative payment transactions and orders Apple to pay 85% of Epic's costs through the original trial. Apple has said it will appeal and seek a stay, and Epic said Fortnite will return to the Australian App Store.

stories.summary: A taskforce called the Sovereign AI Leadership (SAIL) group, which includes Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco, has asked the Labour government to create a compact offering local communities greater benefits from datacentres. It warns the UK has roughly 12 months to avoid US-style opposition that has halted projects. Proposals include letting councils keep more business rate revenue and an indicative contribution scaled to site size. Opponents, including PauseAI UK, Action to Protect Rural Scotland and Foxglove, criticised the plans. The government said it has already allowed councils in AI growth zones in England to keep all extra business rates and that community benefits are considered through local planning.
key_points: The SAIL taskforce, including Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco, has submitted proposals to ministers.
It warns the UK has about 12 months to build public consent before US-style opposition takes hold.

stories.claim: An Australian court ordered Apple to open iOS to rival app stores and payment systems from March 2027; Apple plans to appeal.
stories.summary: Australia's Federal Court has ordered Apple to open iOS to alternative app marketplaces and payment services from 1 March 2027. stories.headline: Francisco Cancino Mexico Spring 2027

stories.headline: Solana’s Alpenglow, its biggest network overhaul since 2020, goes live Wednesday
stories.claim: Solana's Alpenglow upgrade, its biggest overhaul since 2020, switches on Wednesday to cut settlement time sharply.
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports that Solana's Alpenglow upgrade goes live on Wednesday, aiming to make transactions irreversible in about 150 milliseconds, down from roughly six seconds. The upgrade moves voting off the chain and bundles votes into certificates that lock in transactions in one or two rounds. Validators would pay a flat admission ticket of 0.8 SOL per epoch instead of vote fees, which the article says is about 60% cheaper. The test network was restarted six times since May and one migration was rolled back before a later one succeeded. The switch takes effect at epoch 1064.
key_points: Alpenglow is scheduled to go live on Wednesday at the start of epoch 1064.
Settlement target is about 150 milliseconds, against roughly six seconds today.

stories.headline: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong
stories.claim: UK government plans tighter rules so only trained professionals can offer high-risk cosmetic procedures, with a ban for under-18s.
stories.summary: The government has set out plans for England to restrict high-risk non-surgical cosmetic procedures, including liquid Brazilian butt lifts, vampire facials and deep chemical peels, to properly trained professionals from 2027. Liquid BBLs would be legally classed as cosmetic surgery so only doctors could perform them. High-risk procedures for under-18s would be banned, and rogue providers would face new criminal offences and fixed fines of up to £4,000. The draft rules now go to consultation before parliament considers them in spring 2027. Health Minister Karin Smyth said the aim was to drive rogue operators out of the market.

Many other frequencies and aircraft types are changed, including a gradual rollout of the four-class A350-900 Allegris cabin. The filing also shifts several routes between A340-300, 787-9, A350-900 and 747-400 aircraft, with some frequencies increased or reduced. stories.headline: 'I started ketamine at 14 and needed nappies at 22' - the rise of young people going to rehab
stories.claim: UK rehab referrals for young people with ketamine addiction have risen sharply, with 112 referrals so far this year.
stories.summary: A BBC report describes a sharp rise in young people seeking rehabilitation for ketamine use in the UK. The drugs charity Kaleidoscope says referrals to its Birchwood facility rose from two in 2021 to 112 so far this year, with most clients aged 18 to 24. Researchers at the University of South Wales are studying the specific needs of this group, as harm from ketamine can develop faster than from alcohol or Class A drugs. Individual stories describe severe bladder damage, cognitive and physical harm and difficulties accessing health services. Estimated illicit use among 16 to 59-year-olds was about 264,000 people in 2024-25.

Most clients are aged 18 to 24, with a rise also seen among adults aged 25 to 34.

stories.claim: Albertans have rejected a binding referendum on separation from Canada, according to early preliminary results.
stories.summary: Preliminary results from Alberta's October 19 vote show about 76.5% backing remaining in Canada and 23.5% backing a referendum on separation. Premier Danielle Smith said no separation referendum would be held while she is in power. Separatist leaders plan to challenge her within the United Conservative Party, though it is unclear whether they have the numbers. The vote also included nine questions on immigration and the constitution.

stories.headline: A young life ‘dominated by gambling’: Victorian coroner delivers stinging findings on death of 22-year-old
stories.claim: A Victorian coroner found online sports betting was the direct cause of a 22-year-old's suicide in 2021.
stories.summary: Victorian coroner Paul Lawrie found that online betting was the direct and paramount cause of the 2021 suicide of Kyle Hudson, a 22-year-old from Werribee. Hudson gambled $895,733 across Sportsbet, Entain and Bet365 over four years. The coroner criticised Sportsbet's position that Hudson had no gambling problem and recommended that the federal government require betting firms to show customers' net losses and fund an independent data vault. He also said monitoring of gambling harm should not rest solely with the companies. The findings add to pressure on the online betting industry in Australia.

stories.headline: NHS trust prosecuted over children's sepsis deaths
stories.claim: An NHS trust is being prosecuted over two children's sepsis deaths at Broomfield Hospital, Essex.
stories.summary: Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust faces three charges brought by the Care Quality Commission over the deaths of two children who had sepsis at Broomfield Hospital. Zadie Ajetunmobi, three, died in November 2022 and was not given intravenous antibiotics for more than seven hours. Selina Samarina, two, who had Down's syndrome, was sent home by a junior doctor in April 2024 and died two days later. The trust said it was working closely with investigators. It is due before Chelmsford Magistrates' Court, with pleas expected on 3 December.

stories.headline: Israel’s elections 2026 explained in maps and charts
stories.claim: Israel holds a general election on 27 October, with Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition in a close race.
stories.summary: Israel votes on 27 October to elect the 26th Knesset, the first general vote to take place at the natural end of a full term in 38 years. Benjamin Netanyahu, seeking another term while on trial for corruption charges he denies, leads a far-right coalition locked in a close race with a Jewish-led opposition bloc. Neither side is on track for the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat parliament. The Supreme Court overturned bans on the Ra'am and Joint List parties, and Arab-led parties could hold the balance of power. Coalition formation could take up to 42 days, and failing that, the country would vote again.
